title: Align addressing spec human IID derivation with canonical SHA-512 native model
description: spec/03-addressing.md normatively says SHA-256(pubkey), and claims the IID is used for ULA/optional GUA, while canonical implementations/vectors/security spec use SHA-512(pubkey)[0:8] with U/L clear, link-local plus exact 0200::/8 native /128, no ULA. Correct the normative derivation and cross-references to eliminate an implementation-splitting contradiction.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD (adopted spec updates, checkpoint 846971f9dc): spec/03-addressing.md normative derivation now SHA-512(pubkey) with U/L clear (:15-16), no ULA - 'ULA addresses (fc00::/7) are not used' with exact native construction addr=[0x02]+SHA-512(pubkey)[0:7]+IID (:22), cross-references 04-network 6.2/12 and 06-security 8.5 intact (:22,:30). Cross-checked: 04-network.md uses SHA-512 unified derivation + 0200::/8 single-primary (no ULA/GUA layering), 06-security.md 8.5 'MUST be SHA-512, not SHA-256' with U/L cleared; repo-wide rg finds no remaining SHA-256(pubkey) normative text in spec/.
